reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - plasma amyloid-beta 1-40 increased dramatically (172,754 vs 263 pg/mL) and plasma amyloid-beta 1-42 increased substantially (18,485 vs 16 pg/mL), consistent with solanezumab binding to amyloid-beta and preventing clearance. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence - CSF amyloid-beta 1-42 showed some decrease (-37.33 vs -9.27 pg/mL) suggesting some central nervous system engagement, but the modified CSF measure increased (315.69 vs -107.91 pg/mL). The biomarker pattern suggests target engagement but unclear downstream pathway effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint clearly missed - ADAS-Cog14 showed no significant improvement (p=0.095, effect size -0.8 points). The trial was adequately powered with 2,129 patients over 80 weeks. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup differences - cognitive responders at both 6-point (35.7% vs 35.3%) and 9-point cutoffs (55.2% vs 52.3%) were essentially identical between arms, as were functional responders (38.0% vs 36.8%). 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major confounders - adequate sample size, appropriate duration for Alzheimer's trials, no safety issues preventing adequate dosing, and placebo response appears normal for this indication.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear target engagement evidenced by massive increases in plasma amyloid-beta levels, but primary cognitive endpoint failed to improve despite adequate power and duration. The biomarker pattern suggests the drug engaged amyloid-beta but this didn't translate to meaningful downstream biological effects on neurodegeneration.
